enriched_description: Cylindrical stick of wax (15-30 cm tall, 2-5 cm diameter) with a central wick (cotton string) extending from the top. The wax body is smooth and uniform, available in white, ivory, or colored varieties. The surface has a matte or slightly glossy finish depending on wax type (paraffin, beeswax, soy). The top has a charred wick tip if previously burned. Taper candles narrow toward the top; pillar candles maintain uniform diameter. The base is flat for standing. Scented candles may have a slightly textured surface from fragrance oils. The overall shape is a simple vertical cylinder with a thin wick protruding from the center.

Heavy artillery piece with a long, thick cylindrical barrel (1-5 meters long, 15-40 cm bore diameter) mounted on a wheeled carriage or tank turret. The barrel is made of cast iron or steel with a matte dark finish. The muzzle end may have a brake or flash suppressor. The breech end has a loading mechanism. The carriage consists of a metal frame with large spoked or solid wheels (historical) or a modern tracked vehicle mount. The overall silhouette is a massive horizontal cylinder elevated at an angle, with the barrel as the dominant feature.

Small, narrow boat (3-6 meters long, 60-90 cm wide) with pointed ends (bow and stern) and an open top. The hull is constructed from wood, aluminum, fiberglass, or plastic, with a smooth exterior surface. The sides curve upward from the waterline to form gunwales. The interior has cross braces (thwarts) for structural support and seating. The hull bottom is flat or slightly V-shaped. Colors range from natural wood tones to painted finishes (red, blue, green, white). The overall silhouette is a slender, elongated oval with symmetrical pointed ends and an open deck.

Handheld tool with a cutting wheel (sharp circular blade) and a rotating gear mechanism. The body consists of two handles (metal or plastic) connected by a pivot, with the cutting wheel and gear positioned between them. The handles are 10-15 cm long with ergonomic grips. The cutting wheel is a small (2-3 cm diameter) hardened steel disc. A magnetic lid catcher may be attached. The overall shape is a compact, hand-sized device with a distinctive cutting head. Manual can openers have a crank handle; electric models have a motorized base with a slot for the can.

Knitted jacket with an open front fastened by buttons, a zipper, or worn open. The garment has long sleeves, a V-neck or round neckline, and a body length extending to the waist or hips. The knit texture is visible, with ribbed cuffs, hem, and collar. Constructed from wool, cotton, or synthetic yarn in solid colors, patterns, or cable-knit designs. Buttons are typically 4-8, spaced evenly down the front. The cardigan drapes loosely over the body, with a relaxed fit. The overall silhouette is a rectangular torso covering with sleeve extensions and a front opening.

Reflective glass surface mounted in a housing (plastic or metal frame) attached to the exterior or interior of a vehicle. Exterior mirrors (side mirrors) are rectangular or slightly curved, 10-20 cm wide, mounted on arms extending from the door or A-pillar. Interior mirrors (rearview) are rectangular (15-25 cm wide) mounted on the windshield with a pivot arm. The reflective surface is flat or convex (exterior) with a silver or blue-tinted coating. The housing is typically black or body-colored plastic. Some models have integrated turn signal indicators.

Large circular rotating platform with a central support column and a decorative canopy roof. The platform (8-15 meters diameter) has mounted seats in the form of carved wooden horses, chariots, or other animals arranged in concentric rings. The horses are painted in bright colors with decorative saddles and bridles. Mirror panels line the central column. The canopy is a domed or conical roof with painted scenes, lights, and ornamental trim. The overall structure is a colorful, ornate circular machine with a festive, carnival aesthetic.

Portable container (toolbox or bag) holding an assortment of carpentry tools. The container is a rectangular box (30-50 cm wide, 20-30 cm tall) made of plastic, metal, or canvas with a handle and latches. Contents typically include a hammer, screwdrivers, tape measure, level, saw, chisels, and nails/screws organized in compartments. The exterior is typically red, black, or yellow with branding. The kit has a utilitarian, organized appearance with tools visible when opened. The overall silhouette is a rectangular box with a carrying handle.

Rectangular box constructed from corrugated cardboard or paperboard with flaps on the top and bottom for closure. The walls are thin (2-5 mm) with a brown (kraft) or printed white exterior surface. Standard sizes range from small (10x10x10 cm) to large (60x40x40 cm). The box has sharp edges and flat faces with visible corrugation lines on cut edges. Tape or staples secure the flaps. Printed labels, barcodes, and handling symbols may be present on the surface. The overall shape is a rectangular prism with a matte, fibrous texture.

Circular assembly consisting of a metal rim (15-22 inches diameter) with a rubber tire mounted around the outer edge. The rim has a central hub with bolt holes (4-8 holes) for attachment to the vehicle. The wheel face features a decorative cover (hubcap) or exposed spokes (alloy wheels). The tire has a tread pattern on the outer surface and sidewall markings. The rim finish is polished aluminum, painted silver, or black. The overall silhouette is a flat disc with a raised outer lip and a recessed center hub.
